text: Finishing starts with sanding. Sand with the grain until the wood feels smooth all over.
Wipe off all the dust before any finish goes on.
Pick the right finish: water-based wipe-on finish for most projects, food-safe oil for things that touch food, and paste wax for a soft shine.
Wear gloves. Put a little finish on a rag and wipe it along the grain in long strokes.
Thin coats are better than thick ones — thick coats drip and stay sticky.
Let it dry. The can says how long — often 2 hours for water-based finish.
Rub lightly with very fine sandpaper and wipe off the dust, then add another coat.

tip.text: Try every finish on a scrap first, or make a finish sampler!

text: Spray cans are for grown-ups: the mist is easy to breathe in and can catch fire.
Oily rags go to your grown-up to lay flat outside or put in water.

tip.text: Open a window or work outside when you put on a finish.
